# Canvas round-trip check, the text to type
#
# Paste each block into the matching module on the lesson page, then Gather and
# submit to Canvas. scripts/verify-canvas-check.js diffs what comes back out of
# the parser against exactly this file.
#
# The content is deliberately awkward. Every character class here has broken a
# copy-paste pipeline somewhere: a curly apostrophe becomes a question mark under
# the wrong encoding, an ampersand comes back as &amp; when an HTML decode is
# missed, a double quote breaks naive CSV, an en dash is the character that once
# silently dropped the Topic field on six lessons, and a blank line between
# paragraphs is what Canvas's editor rewrites on the way in and again on the way
# out. Long answers are here because truncation is the failure mode that looks
# like a student writing less than they did.
#
# Lines starting with # are ignored. A slot header is ==slot-id==.

==map-check-response==
The Grand Canal linked the Huai and Yangzi systems, and the state's grain tax moved north along it.

That mattered because the capital could feed an army it had no local means to supply — the canal is the reason the northern frontier was defensible at all. Roughly 40% of the tax grain travelled this way.

==first10-q1==
Champa rice ripened in about 60 days, so a farmer could take two harvests where one had been possible; the "double-cropping" that followed is what drove the population past 100 million.

==first10-q2==
What continued was the Confucian claim that a well-ordered family models a well-ordered state. What changed was who could act on it: the examination system meant a merchant's son might outrank a general's.

==first10-q3==
Trade shifted seaward. The Indian Ocean routes carried bulk goods (porcelain, iron, salt) that the overland routes never could, and Quanzhou's harbour records show ships from Srivijaya, the Chola lands & the Abbasid ports.

==skill-builder-response==
Cause: Champa rice and the canal together produced a surplus.
Effect: cities grew past what local farmland could support.

The link runs through distribution, not through agriculture alone — a surplus that cannot move is not a surplus, it is a glut. This is why I would rank the canal above the rice.

==checkpoint-one-response==
The Song staffed government through civil service exams rather than birth, which produced scholar-officials loyal to the bureaucracy and to the emperor instead of to regional lords. Neo-Confucianism gave that arrangement its justification, and the Mandate of Heaven gave it a way to explain failure without abandoning the system.

==evidence-response==
The scroll shows shopfronts opening directly onto the street, with no compound wall between the seller and the buyer. That is a market economy operating in public, not a controlled market district, and it is the single clearest visual argument for Song commercialisation.

==primary-source-response==
A Song official wrote it, and the audience was the court, so the tone is advisory rather than descriptive. He has an interest in the reforms succeeding; "the people rejoice" is the sort of claim I would want a second source for before I used it.

==checkpoint-two-response==
Continuity: the Confucian social hierarchy, with the scholar above the farmer, the artisan and the merchant.

Change: an economy that had made some merchants richer than most scholars, which the hierarchy had no language for. The Song did not resolve that tension; they inherited it and passed it on.
